To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dynorphin 13-mer peptide analog [D-Ala(2), (F5)PHE(4)]-dynorphin 13-NH(2) (DAFPH) is a potent and selective kappa opioid peptide agonist.
the dynorphin A analog, [D-A1a2,(F 5)Phe 4 ]-dynorphin A 1–13-N H 2 (DAF PHEDYN), was found to be a potent and highly kappa-selective agonist in vivo and in vitro.

the analog, [D-alanine(2), 4-(F5) phenylalanine]dynorphin1-13-N-ethylamide, was found to be 10-fold more potent than the parent compound, dynorphin1- 13, in inducing diuresis, analgesia, and hypothermia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a dynorphin analog which is more potent than the parent compound, retains kappa selectivity, and is orally active.
the synthesis and biological evaluation of dynorphin analogs.
the development of potent and selective kappa opioid agonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this new dynorphin analog exhibits marked in vivo selectivity for the opioid kappa receptor.
the DAFPHDYN is a potent and selective kappa opioid agonist.
the DAFPHENYL derivative of dynorphin is a potent kappa opioid agonist.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DAFPHEDYND is a potent analog of the opioid peptide, dynorphin 11-13.
DAFPHEDYNDYN is a potent kappa opioid agonist and that the D-Ala2 substitution is responsible for the increased potency.
DAFPHEDYIN is a potent analog of dynorhpin 1-13.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the F5 substitution at the Phe4 position of dynorphin1–11 is a useful strategy for increasing the potency of dynorphin analogs.
the F5 modification to Phe4 in dynorphin 13-17 results in a potent dynorphin 11-13 analog that has a similar selectivity as dynorphin 17-13.
the substitution of a fluorine for the hydrogen at the 2 position of the phenylalanine at the fourth position of dynorphin results in a compound with a marked increase in potency.
